title: Socio-demographic and lifestyle influences on falls among the elderly in Gatanga Sub-County
author: Ernest Kimani
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.zwyf7fw
materials: Highest Level of education attained (Githomo Kinene)(Select one)
Secondary completed (Kurikia gia secondary/ gia keri)

steps.title: Screen Participants for Eligibility
steps.instruction: Verify that the potential participant meets all the following criteria before proceeding with the interview:

substeps.instruction: Age: Must be 65 years and above as of the interview date.
Residency: Must have resided in Gatanga sub-county for the last 1 year.
Physical Ability: No physical disability limiting walking with both legs or limiting the use of arms for balance and support.
Mental State: Must be able to correctly identify the present time of day, their physical location, and themselves by at least two names.
Functional Ability: Must be able to perform self-feeding, self-bathroom, and self-grooming activities.
Behavior: Must maintain normal interaction with close contacts and the interviewer, devoid of bizarre behavior.

steps.title: Assess Medical History and Current Health
steps.instruction: Determine if the participant has sought medical care for specific conditions in the last 12 months and record the duration of illness where applicable.

substeps.instruction: Screen for: Diabetes, Hypertension (record duration in years/months), Heart Disease, Lung disease, Kidney disease, and Anemia.
Screen for Arthritis/Joint pains in: Hip, Knees, Ankle, Foot, Wrist, Fingers, Elbow, and Shoulder.
Screen for: Lower Back pain, Neck pains, Dizziness, Headache, Altered Mental States/dementia, Acute stress/depressed mood, Memory loss, and Stroke.
Screen for Fractures and specify type: ankle, leg, femur, hip, forearm, or humerus.
Screen for Visual impairment (reduced vision), use of Glasses, and Blindness (one eye or both eyes).
Screen for Hearing impairment and Peripheral Neuropathy.
Screen for Bruises, cuts, Wounds, and pressure sores.
Assess for: Unsteadiness in gait/balance problems, difficulty in carrying out usual activities, acute illness, and hospital admission.

steps.title: Document Medication and Lifestyle Factors
steps.instruction: Collect data on current medications, substance use, and home environment.

substeps.instruction: Record if the participant is currently on any medication/drugs and specify the illness for which they are taken.
Assess alcohol consumption: record if they drink, the type of drinker, number of days per month, and number of bottles/glasses per sitting.
Assess cigarette smoking: record if they smoke, the type of smoker, and other relevant usage information.
Identify if assistive walking devices are used.
Record the type of house floor and the main source of lighting at night.
Identify primary cohabitants (e.g., spouse, child, brother/sister) and the presence of domestic animals.
Document daily activities and nutritional habits (specifically if they consume at least 3 meals daily).
If fewer than 3 meals are consumed, record the reason: lack of food, lack of someone to cook, or lack of appetite due to illness.
Record the method of payment for treatment and hospital bills (e.g., NHIF or other insurance).

steps.title: Evaluate Fall History and Outcomes
steps.instruction: Determine the occurrence and impact of falls since the participant reached age 65, focusing on the last 12 months.

substeps.instruction: Ask if the participant has ever fallen since age 65.
Ask if the participant has fallen in the last 12 months. If NO, proceed directly to FiND, MNA-SF, and Modified Barthel Index forms.
If YES, record the number of falls in the last 12 months.
For the last episode, record the location: Inside House, Within Compound but outside house, or In the garden.
Record the terrain of the fall.
Document outcomes of the fall: reason for fall, occurrence of blackout, head injury, or fractures (specify Femur/thigh, Radius-ulna/forearm, or Humerus/upper arm and specify Right or Left side).
Record presence of skin bruises/lacerations, hospitalization, fear of falling, immobilization, abandonment of daily activities, loss of autonomy, or confusion.
Record if the participant was accompanied during the fall, the time of the fall, and the immediate pre- and post-fall circumstances (including triggering events or alcohol influence).

steps.title: Perform Functional Assessments
steps.instruction: Complete the Mini Nutritional Assessment (MNA-SF) and the Barthel Index of Activities of Daily Living.

substeps.instruction: Administer the Mini Nutritional Assessment – short form (Kikuyu Translation).
Score the Barthel Index based on actual (not potential) functioning over the preceding 24–48 hours using self-reports, relative reports, or observation.

Score the following 10 items: Bowel control (0-1), Bladder control (0-2), Grooming (0-1), Dressing (0-2), Eating (0-2), Transfer from bed to chair (0-2), Ambulation/Mobility (1-3), Bathing (0-1), and Toilet use (0-2).
Apply Barthel Index guidelines: Unconscious patients score '0'; use of aids is allowed for independence; catheterized patients who manage the catheter alone are 'continent'.
